newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says no plan to probe losses on foreign bonds.
newsitem.headline: MOF says no plan to probe losses on foreign bonds.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) currently has no plans to investigate foreign bond sales by Japanese brokerages after the dollar's recent fall caused private investors who bought the bonds to suffer huge losses, officials at the ministry said on Friday.
Financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Friday that MOF was planning to investigate domestic brokerages that sold foreign bonds to private investors.
"We have no plans to investigate brokerages over their foreign bond sales activity at this point," a MOF official said.
He said MOF was not in a position to interfere with brokerages' sales activities related to foreign bond offerings as long as they were not illegal.
Nihon Keizai said the dollar's sudden reversal had forced individual investors to swallow losses shortly after they had bought foreign bonds.
It said many brokerages had to cancel offerings during the subscription period for foreign bonds that had fallen below their face value because of the dollar's fall.
The dive in the dollar also caused heavy losses for private investors, particularly on dual-currency foreign bonds that contained special foreign exchange option terms, market sources said.
Such option-linked bonds enable bond holders to receive high coupons in yen at maturity only if foreign exchange rates stay above levels agreed at the time of the launch.
The coupon of such dual-currency bonds is paid in yen, while the bonds, usually with maturities of three to six months, are redeemed in foreign currencies.
The bonds are profitable as long as foreign exchange rates do not fall below a certain level, but investors incur heavy losses if rates break below that level.
The so-called "knockout" dollar level for most of the options is estimated to have been set at 118 to 120 yen, with some at 115 to 117 yen, currency traders said.

"There is an official guideline by the JSDA (Japan Securities Dealers' Association) that establishes rules for foreign bond sales. We are assuming that each firm is taking full responsibility for abiding by the rules," the official said.

"Basically, we will only act when problems actually occur," the official said. "As long as brokerages follow the guideline properly, we have to say that responsibility lies with the investors themselves."

Regarding the foreign exchange option-linked dual-currency bonds that caused investors huge losses, he said: "As long as the investors recognise the risks that are involved in such instruments, we have no right to restrict them altogether."
He said investors have a right to choose risky instruments for their investments.
